target:
def Target : Prop :=
  ∀ (m : ℕ) [NeZero m] (k : ℕ) (N : S1 Bool Bool),
    N.D12 → N.D25 k → S1.D6 N (d26 m) →
    m ∣ k.factorial ^ N.d13
a_raw: {"translation": "Target defines the following proposition (it names the proposition without asserting or proving it): For every nonzero natural number m (m : ℕ with m ≠ 0), every natural number k, and every finite-component Boolean-input, Boolean-output system N of type S1 Bool Bool — consisting of a finite type A1 of nodes, a local state type A3 n for each node n in A1, an initial state a4 n in A3 n for each node n, a node update function a5 taking a node n, a global state assignment σ : (j : A1) → A3 j, and a Boolean input x to a new value in A3 n, and an output function a6 mapping a global state assignment to a Boolean — if all three of the following hypotheses hold: (1) defining a direct dependency edge a → b between nodes a, b in A1 to hold when there exist two global state assignments σ and σ' that agree on every node other than a and a Boolean input x such that a5 b σ x ≠ a5 b σ' x, there are no two distinct nodes n₁ ≠ n₂ in A1 such that there is both a nonempty chain (length ≥ 1) of direct dependency edges from n₁ to n₂ and a nonempty chain of direct dependency edges from n₂ to n₁ (note that self-dependencies n → n are allowed; only cycles containing at least two distinct nodes are excluded); (2) for every node n in A1, the local state type A3 n is finite and has at most k elements; and (3) for every finite list xs of Booleans (of any length, including the empty list), N produces the same Boolean output as the system d26 m — where a system's output on xs is obtained by starting from its initial global state a4, updating all nodes synchronously left-to-right for each Boolean in xs, and applying a6 to the resulting global state, and where d26 m is the single-node system (index type Unit) whose state type is Fin m = {0, …, m - 1}, whose initial state is 0, whose update rule adds 1 modulo m on input true and leaves the state unchanged on input false, and whose output is true if the state equals 0 and false otherwise (equivalently, d26 m outputs true on xs if and only if m divides the number of true entries in xs) — then m divides (k!) ^ |A1|, where k! is the factorial of k and |A1| is the cardinality of N's finite node type A1. No other assumptions are imposed (in particular, A1 is not required to be nonempty, different nodes may have different local state types, and k may be any natural number including 0)."}

only cycles containing at least two distinct nodes are excluded); (2) for every node n in A1, the local state type A3 n is finite and has at most k elements; and (3) for every finite list xs of Booleans (of any length, including the empty list), N produces the same Boolean output as the system d26 m — where a system's output on xs is obtained by starting from its initial global state a4, updating all nodes synchronously left-to-right for each Boolean in xs, and applying a6 to the resulting global state, and where d26 m is the single-node system (index type Unit) whose state type is Fin m = {0, …, m - 1}, whose initial state is 0, whose update rule adds 1 modulo m on input true and leaves the state unchanged on input false, and whose output is true if the state equals 0 and false otherwise (equivalently, d26 m outputs true on xs if and only if m divides the number of true entries in xs) — then m divides (k!) ^ |A1|, where k! is the factorial of k and |A1| is the cardinality of N's finite node type A1. divergences.description: The description refers simply to 'the counter modulo m' without specifying its input/output interface, whereas the Lean target fixes d26 m : S1 Bool Bool to take Boolean inputs (true increments modulo m, false holds the state) and output a Boolean indicator of whether the count is 0 mod m (decide (σ () = 0)), rather than outputting the residue in Fin m or taking unary input. This is a benign formalization choice (in fact, requiring agreement only with the zero-indicator output yields a stronger theorem that implies the Fin m-output and unary-input versions).

The Lean formalizes 'a network' as a deterministic, synchronous discrete-time Moore machine with a finite set of units, fixed initial state, and an unrestricted global readout function (S1 Bool Bool), and defines inter-unit feedback (D12 via D7) using functional dependence quantified over all global states (including unreachable ones), with self-loops permitted. While this matches the paper's causal architecture well, these architectural specifics are left implicit in the English description.

judgement.summary: The Lean target faithfully captures the author's stated divisibility condition for feed-forward networks realizing a mod-m counter, and the description accurately characterizes its relation to the passages without misreporting them. There are only minor specification choices left implicit in the English summary, chiefly that the mod-m counter is formalized with Boolean inputs and a Boolean zero-detector output.
